standard_prerequisites.name: The characterisation of modules that are summands of direct sums of modules R/fR
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the required summand statement into the surjectivity of a Hom map for all short exact sequences of the stated form.

standard_prerequisites.name: Localization of modules and of Hom out of a finitely presented module
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets surjectivity be checked at maximal ideals and identifies the localized Hom modules.

standard_prerequisites.name: The structure of finitely presented modules over a ring whose localizations satisfy the generalized valuation ring conditions
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the direct sum decomposition of M_m that makes the localized map surjective.

core_obligations: Reduce to proving that Hom_R(M, B) -> Hom_R(M, C) is surjective for every short exact sequence 0 -> A -> B -> C -> 0 with fA = A cap fB for all f in R, using the preceding module-characterisation lemma (proof lines 37749-37757).
Show it suffices to prove this after localization at maximal ideals, invoking the criterion for a map of modules to be an isomorphism in terms of its localizations (proof lines 37758-37760).

Verify that the localized sequences 0 -> A_m -> B_m -> C_m -> 0 satisfy fA_m = A_m cap fB_m for all f in R_m, using that f can be written u f' with u a unit of R_m and f' in R, and that localization is exact (proof lines 37761-37766).
Use finite presentation of M to localize the Hom modules: Hom_R(M, B)_m = Hom_{R_m}(M_m, B_m) and Hom_R(M, C)_m = Hom_{R_m}(M_m, C_m) (proof lines 37767-37772).

Apply the hypothesis at the maximal ideal together with the lemma describing modules over a generalized valuation ring, concluding that M_m is a direct sum of modules R_m/fR_m and hence by the characterisation lemma that the localized map is surjective (proof lines 37773-37778).
Conclude the finiteness step: since M is a finite R-module, its image in the direct sum of the R/f_i R lies in the sub-sum over a finite subset of the index set (proof lines 37780-37785).
difficulty_reason: The lemma assumes that every local ring of R at a maximal ideal satisfies the equivalent conditions of the generalized-valuation-ring lemma, and concludes that every finitely presented R-module is a summand of a finite direct sum of modules of the form R/fR (source lines 37736-37746). The proof is a genuine local-to-global argument. It reduces the conclusion to showing that Hom_R(M, B) -> Hom_R(M, C) is surjective for every short exact sequence with the property fA = A cap fB for all f, which is the characterisation established by the preceding module lemma (proof lines 37749-37757). Surjectivity is then checked after localization at maximal ideals, using that the localized sequences inherit the condition because an element of a localization can be written as a unit times an element of R and localization is exact, and using that the Hom modules localize for finitely presented M (proof lines 37758-37772). The conclusion at each maximal ideal is exactly the hypothesis, reduced through the localized modules lemma (proof lines 37773-37778). The final step is what makes the direct sum finite: since M is a finite R-module its image in the potentially infinite direct sum lies in a finite sub-sum (proof lines 37780-37785). The two non-routine moves are the localization of the condition fA = A cap fB and the finiteness bookkeeping at the end.
